Scope lists five file groups; diff also touches usePacientesList.js and factory-setup.test.js (route count 8→10) without listing them
insertRunning fail-open still calls updateFinished with the in-memory id, so a failed insert overwrites another kind's persisted row
pino formatter emits textual status, then HTTP status in the same key overwrites it; Datadog JSON parse keeps 404/200 instead of info/warn

unresolved: CI-only comment+status both insert kind=verdict (comment live/audit null, status SKIP/SKIP); host collectEvents reproduces two rows; already in MotherDuck (e.g. PR 2786 / 6410f996). writeEvents is INSERT OR REPLACE, so stopping emission leaves legacy rows; the weekly query must collapse that state without DELETE to hide the failure
Referenced send after Usar bypasses the parent sending lock; two clicks or two Enters before re-render both POST /send and GHL can deliver twice because usable() ignores sent_message_id.
sendUsed success always setSendReference(null) and setOverlay without a convRef check, so a late send on A wipes B's restored send reference and the next send on B takes the unreferenced onSend path.
Referenced send that finishes after a conversation switch leaves a pending overlay; returning to A shows a stuck pending bubble and retry is a no-op because the reference was deleted on success.
economy classify sends every PR into Trail check mode, which posts verdict and arms squash auto-merge without reading needs-victor

Unresolved: localVerifierRounds returns [] for the actual local PASS+NOTES verdict on PR #2842. The regex requires compact JSON with adjacent verdict/head fields and no newline before mode; valid spaced or multiline contract JSON is discarded, so the reader receives Local verifier rounds: 0. Parse the fenced JSON structurally.

Unresolved: matches preserves inventory order, which groups Claude before Codex rather than sorting sessions by launch time. A Claude verification at 13:00 followed in inventory by a Codex verification at 12:00 produces [second.jsonl, first.jsonl]. run.js labels those files trail-1 and trail-2 and tells the reader they are in round order, reversing the chronology used to judge verifier-false-fail/verifier-miss. Sort the matched rounds by session launch time before numbering.

unresolved: the body says of initiatives, project label groups, project statuses, views and auto-archive that 'none is reachable through the MCP', and the shipped doc repeats 'label groups ... are not on the MCP'; the hosted Linear MCP exposes mcp__linear__save_project_label {name, isGroup, parent} (plus list/retire/restore_project_label with includeGroups), which creates a label group and its children, so the quantifier is false for label groups and the §Admin section routes an MCP-native operation through the raw-key door; the other four objects are absent from the MCP as stated (Tradeoffs already lists only those four)

Unresolved: when conversation sync has a newer inbound summary but message sync has not caught up, the unconditional cached-body preference replaces the fresh summary with an older preview. Base returns NEW inbound at 12:00; head returns OLD cached from 11:00 with the 12:00 date. Prefer the cache only when it represents the latest real message, accounting for summary timestamp drift.

Unresolved: migration stamps every GHL conversation as polled, including a conversation older than 720h with no cached messages. Base selects that conversation; migrated head selects no target, so its existing history stays missing until another summary advance or recent activity. Do not seed a successful poll for a conversation whose messages were never fetched. This differs from the documented exclusion of new outbound messages on dormant threads.

Unresolved, also acknowledged under Tradeoffs: the connector durably stamps the poll before yielding messages to DataEngine. Stop after the first yield and before the engine commits its buffer for a newly imported cold conversation: base retries the missing message, head makes no second request, and both caches still contain zero messages. Commit the poll marker with the fetched records, or retain a retry condition for an incomplete commit.

Unresolved: migration treats any cached message as proof that the current summary was polled. For a conversation with Jan 1 summary and only a Dec 1 cached message, base selects it; migrated head stamps Jan 1 and skips it outside 720h. The missing Jan 1 message remains unfetched until the summary advances or recent activity returns. Preserve eligibility when existing cache does not cover the source summary, or close a real poll before seeding. This differs from the documented exclusion of future outbound sends on dormant threads.

Unresolved: on a Codex lead under economy, model --role local verifier resolves Sol through the native Codex route, so the result has route.native but no route.cli or route.model. Step 3 requires the absent fields to select and fill an external launch command, leaving the local Verifier unlaunchable from an explicitly supported Codex lead. Resolve a headless launch route explicitly and cover the exact playbook-facing output.

Unresolved: repeated documented task --role calls derive the same ID, and enqueue returns the stale row instead of launching the new child; this breaks repeated loop attempts and fresh playbook activations.
Unresolved: the flat token scan blocks safe commands whose argument is a launcher name (for example rg codex) while allowing a quoted nested launch such as sh -c 'codex exec hi'.
Unresolved: steps that explicitly spawn PR owners have no [child] marker, so step done admits them with an empty child registry; the stated playbook backstop is incomplete.
Unresolved: shell operators are discarded before only one primary token is inspected, so true && codex exec hi, a semicolon plus claude, and a pipe to grok are allowed in a carrier pane.
Unresolved: env -i codex exec hi is allowed because wrapper parsing stops at the env option, so a primary Codex launch escapes the carrier guard.
Unresolved: node tools/learnings/run.js && codex exec hi is allowed because the learnings exemption is applied to the merged command instead of only its own shell segment.
